issues.title: LLVM Weekly - #672, November 16th 2026
issues.html:
LLVM Weekly - #672, November 16th 2026

Welcome to the six hundred and seventy-second issue of LLVM Weekly, a weekly newsletter (published every Monday) covering developments in LLVM, Clang, and related projects. LLVM Weekly is brought to you by Alex Bradbury. Subscribe to future issues at https://llvmweekly.org and pass it on to anyone else you think may be interested. Please send any tips or feedback via email: asb@asbradbury.org, or Mastodon: @llvmweekly@fosstodon.org / @asb@fosstodon.org, or Bluesky: @llvmweekly.org / @asbradbury.org.

News and articles from around the web and events

Iason Karaprodromidis wrote on the LLVM project blog about their GSoC project to add Fortran support to LLDB.

Save the date for EuroLLVM 2027, taking place April 26-28th in Porto. The call for program committee volunteers is open now.

The Meta engineering blog posted about extending LLDB to debug applications that span CPUs and GPUs.

The website for LLVM libc has had a redesign and now gives completeness metrics for each header.

Recordings are now available from the GNU Tools Cauldron 2026.

The next Israel LLVM Meetup will take place on November 24th.

According to the LLVM Calendar in the coming week there will be the following:

  • Office hours with the following hosts: Phoebe Wang, Clang maintainers.
  • Online sync-ups on the following topics: formal specification, pointer authentication, lifetime safety, vectoriser improvements, Flang, RISC-V, LLVM libc, HLSL, LLVM libc math.
  • For more details see the LLVM calendar, getting involved documentation on online sync ups and office hours.

On the forums

  • Eugen Zalenko proposes to limit the rate of AI/bot-assisted issue creation.

  • Aaron Ballman is interested in starting a community floating-point working group.

  • Round table notes are now up for compact unwind on ELF.

  • Louis Dionne provided an update on work on LNT v5.

  • Harrison Hao posted an RFC on deprecating and removing support for the R600/TeraScale, having confirmed that Mesa no longer depends on it.

  • Matthias Springer proposed a new ub.assume operation in MLIR.

  • Slava Zakharin posted an RFC (and linked a design document) on representing Fortran aliasing rules in LLVM IR.

  • Andrzej Warzyński and Vicky Nguyen proposed extending update_cc_test_checks.py to support tests that verify multiple IRs within a single source file.

  • Madhur Amilkanthwar, Sjoerd Meijer, Sebastian Pop, Elvina Yakubova, and Yafet Beyene shared an RFC on communicating array extents to LLVM using llvm.assume.chained. “Fortran guarantees that every array subscript stays within its dimension, but the guarantee is lost when Flang lowers an access to a linear address. We propose llvm.assume.chained, a pointer-forwarding intrinsic whose operand bundles carry an array’s extents and strides from Flang to delinearization and dependence analysis. Accesses use the returned pointer as their base, so they retain the array information when passes rebuild loads and stores. We also implemented the same facts as bundles on the existing llvm.assume, one per access: both reach the same loop interchanges and runtime gains, but the chained intrinsic does so at a lower compile-time cost. We compare the two, along with instruction metadata.”

  • Alina Sbirlea would like to host LLVM formal verification tools as part of the LLVM project. i.e. a central repository of shared input test cases paired with expected tool outputs. There was some discussion about how useful this collection of test cases would be, vs bringing in more tools to the monorepo, vs providing a compiler explorer instance.

  • Andrzej Warzyński and Federico Bruzzone are seeking to align MLIR CODEOWNERS with those who are actively reviewing.

  • Kay Hicketts and Valentyn Yukhymenko shared an RFC on user-defined annotations for static analysis. This would provide an annotation mechanism that lets library owners describe how their APIs should be interpreted by tools such as clang-tidy.

  • Md Abdullah Shahneous Bari started a discussion on changing the handling of fast-math flags on MLIR linalg and vector ops.

  • Caleb Zulawski kicked off an RFC thread on adding an intrinsic to query enabled target features after inlining. Nikita Popov clarified this would be used for the compile-time detection case, for situations where runtime detection is too expensive.

LLVM commits

  • An llvm.vector.shuffle intrinsic was added. 47e4e82.

  • The IRBuilder now supports GEP canonicalisation, where arbitrary GEPs are converted into a sequence of ptradd or scaled ptradd. It was additionally enabled by default. ede30f6, 847ab25.

  • The LangRef data race definition was relaxed. 4687e1e.

  • The way backends handle undefined values was documented. df0a91f.

  • MC layer support, intrinsics, builtins, and instruction selection support was added for the Hexagon HLX (eLementwise eXtension) instructions. 23df5cc, 96e9c10.

  • MC layer support was added for the Hexagon Matrix eXtensions (HMX). 34f2fb6.

  • optnone now implies noinline. 473f6ad.

Clang commits

  • Clang now supports multiple in-process cc1 jobs in a ToolSession. This can be used to support multi-file compilation in the browser in Wasm. cbf54d6.

  • RISC-V XSfmm ABI attributes are supported, which describe whether a function reads/writes matrix state. 09dcbfb.

Other project commits

  • CopyProf can now intercept C heap functions, new/delete, and track per-object cost. 0a215fa, 5e721ed.

  • LLDB now supports standalone line tables in DWARF (i.e. .debug_line without .debug_info). 4f28d96.

  • MLIR docs gained guidance on “non observable” side effect modeling. fd1c6ca.


Subscribe at LLVMWeekly.org.

issues.title: LLVM Weekly - #671, November 9th 2026
issues.html:
LLVM Weekly - #671, November 9th 2026

Welcome to the six hundred and seventy-first issue of LLVM Weekly, a weekly newsletter (published every Monday) covering developments in LLVM, Clang, and related projects. LLVM Weekly is brought to you by Alex Bradbury. Subscribe to future issues at https://llvmweekly.org and pass it on to anyone else you think may be interested. Please send any tips or feedback via email: asb@asbradbury.org, or Mastodon: @llvmweekly@fosstodon.org / @asb@fosstodon.org, or Bluesky: @llvmweekly.org / @asbradbury.org.

News and articles from around the web and events

Benedek Kaibás wrote on the LLVM project blog about their GSoC project to teach the Clang Static Analyzer to understand lifetime annotations.

Sukumar Sawant wrote on the LLVM project blog about their GSoC project to enable float80/float128 on unsupported targets for LLVM libc.

The next Toronto LLVM meetup will take place on 12th November. It will feature two presentations: “Getting started with LLVM (it’s not that scary!)” by Ayokunle Amodu and “From OpenMP to Offload: Lowering Safe Rust to GPUs” by Manuel Drehwald.

As a reminder, the call for presentations for the FOSDEM 2027 LLVM and MLIR devrooms closes on 22nd November.

According to the LLVM Calendar in the coming week there will be the following:

  • Office hours with the following hosts: Alexey Bader, Clang maintainers.
  • Online sync-ups on the following topics: Flang, LLVM qualification group, massive binary working group, modules, LLVM/Offload, BOLT, OpenMP for Flang, HLSL, reflection.
  • For more details see the LLVM calendar, getting involved documentation on online sync ups and office hours.

On the forums

  • Reid Kleckner kicked off a debate on PR limits for non-committers, noting that limiting the number of open PRs for contributors without write access might be one way of rate limiting the incoming (often AI-assisted) PRs.

  • Lewis Crawford started an RFC discussion about consistent denormal flushing during constant folding.

  • Fangrui Song shared details of how LLVM library maintainers can help with the transition to declaring cl:: options in TableGen.

  • Many more LLVM Dev Meeting roundtable or workshop notes have been posted: runtimes workshop, Flang round table, X86 roundtable, InstructionCost roundtable, SelectionDAG roundtable, LLVM libc roundtable, formal specifications round table, and loop transformations round table.

  • Joseph Huber posted an RFC on adding a device address sanitizer for GPUs. DASan would provide fast low-overhead address sanitisation for AMD GPUs, avoiding the need for shadow memory.

  • LLVM 23.1.5 was released.

  • Aaron Ballman shared a summary from the recent discussion on library layering of Parser and Sema in Clang. In short: the status quo for the libraries will remain, but there will be a follow-up meeting to further discuss Sema using the Parser to generate AST nodes.

  • Eli Friedman shared an update on the implementation status of LTO with linker scripts along with a link to the first PR up for review.

  • Jeremy Morse is seeking feedback on plans to sunset the ‘old’ way of representing variable locations after instruction selection.

LLVM commits

  • A ConcurrencySanitizer LLVM pass was added. c4c853f.

  • The loop vectoriser gained support for tail folding vector epilogue loops. 541cafd.

  • tracksRegLiveness was made true by default. 5294924.

  • A SPIR-V target ABI classifier was added to the LLVM ABI library. 12e5222.

  • -verify-machineinstrs was removed from MachineIR tests as llc now verifies the output by default. 2d7136e, 864850e.

  • TableGen now caches instregex patterns to avoid repeated lookups. a68936f.

  • MC layer support was added for the Zyhybrid RISC-V extension (part of CHERI support). 743905e1.

  • A scheduling model was added for the Leon5 SPARC processor. 7517bcd.

Clang commits

  • The -fsanitizer=concurrency option was introduced. 9ac8620.

  • A BoundsSafety index page was added and the upstreaming status was documented. 4aaea35.

  • A ClangIR pass was added to fold empty branches. a100bd4.

Other project commits

  • A CheckedPtr wrapper around unique_ptr was added to LLVM’s libc. 8207e69.

  • arm64e pointer authentication support was added to the MachO LLD linker. b1dc6f6.

  • A MicrosoftABIRuntime was added to LLDB for resolving dynamic values in C++ on the Microsoft ABI. 08458ae.

  • MemProf metadata is now supported in MLIR’s LLVM dialect. 4754186.


Subscribe at LLVMWeekly.org.

issues.title: LLVM Weekly - #670, November 2nd 2026
issues.html:
LLVM Weekly - #670, November 2nd 2026

Welcome to the six hundred and seventieth issue of LLVM Weekly, a weekly newsletter (published every Monday) covering developments in LLVM, Clang, and related projects. LLVM Weekly is brought to you by Alex Bradbury. Subscribe to future issues at https://llvmweekly.org and pass it on to anyone else you think may be interested. Please send any tips or feedback via email: asb@asbradbury.org, or Mastodon: @llvmweekly@fosstodon.org / @asb@fosstodon.org, or Bluesky: @llvmweekly.org / @asbradbury.org.

News and articles from around the web and events

Timm Baeder gave a Clang bytecode interpreter update on the Red Hat blog.

Saleem Abdulrasool wrote about ABIs on the Browser Company Speaking in Swift blog.

According to the LLVM Calendar in the coming week there will be the following:

  • Office hours with the following hosts: Quentin Colombet, Renato Golin.
  • Online sync-ups on the following topics: formal specification, MLIR C/C++ frontend working group, pointer authentication, lifetime safety, Clang static analysis, OpenMP, Clang C and C++ language working group, Flang, RISC-V, LLVM embedded toolchains, HLSL, MLGO, LLVM libc math.
  • For more details see the LLVM calendar, getting involved documentation on online sync ups and office hours.

On the forums

  • Anton Korobeynikov noted that the Graphite review tool will be disabled for the LLVM project as they no longer offer discounted or free plans for open source organisations.

  • Notes are available from various round tables / workshops at last week’s Dev Meeting: debug info, LLVM hearts ML, and the RISC-V roundtable.

  • Michael Kruse provided an update on the effort to improve Flang compilation speed by de-templatising noting that a key PR will land soon. “Flang should not behave any differently, but builds up to 46% faster (gcc, without precompiled headers)”.

  • Ralf Jung started an RFC discussion on adding a freezing memcpy which would be part of the story for exposing freeze to programmers in Rust.

  • Joshua Haberman posted an RFC on tail_chaincc, a maximum efficiency tailcall convention. It combines the callee-cleanup mechanics of tailcc with the register optimisations of preserve_none and is intended to be used with [[clang::musttail]].

  • paperchalice wrote a v2 RFC on TableGen support for RegisterBankInfo, providing a way to define register bank mapping rules by matching TypedOperands.

  • Federico Bruzzone posted an MLIR RFC on unifying masking in the Vector dialect.

  • Konstantin Zhuravlyov started a discussion on vendor-owned pre-merge testing for LLVM PRs.

LLVM commits

  • LoopStrengthReduce learned to rewrite branches to eq/ne with an immediate for targets like RISC-V with the Zibi (immediate branch extension) enabled. 0b56c8e.

  • llvm-dwarfutil now supports --compress-debug-sections. cc6b3b5.

  • An X86 pass was added to insert sfence after non-temporal stores. 238ef21.

  • A number of fixes were made to tail call support on AArch64 Windows. 3c956bd.

  • The ‘debugger-tuning’ module flag was introduced. 738215b.

  • LLVM’s AI contribution policy is now referenced on the ‘how to submit a bug’ page. 5661d4f.

  • llvm.raw.sections named metadata was added for embedding arbitrary binary data into named sections of the output object file. 39cd74f.

  • The LiveVariables analysis was removed, described as “12 years overdue” in the commit message! 93f05d7.

  • Malloc promotion was removed due to being buggy and rarely profitable. e2089b0d.

  • VPlan now computes branch costs. 999b73d.

Clang commits

  • std::meta::is_type support was implemented. 6006957.

  • Clang’s DepScan gained a new API to find modulemaps without loading. ff065cf.

Other project commits

  • Bolt’s webpage styling was updated. d35f657b.

  • LLVM’s libc now has double precision sinh, cosh, and tanh correctly rounded for all rounding modes. 1866d4c, 075a6cb, ff9ad99.

  • LLVM libc’s regex implementation is being fleshed out. ad46922, adb8031.


Subscribe at LLVMWeekly.org.
